---
title: "Talk with Reachy: Privacy Policy"
date: 2026-10-01
---

Talk with Reachy is research software for a Reachy Mini robot used in a study at the University of Cincinnati (principal investigator: Renkai Ma). This page explains what the software does with Google account data.

## Access to your Google account

The software asks for one Google permission, `drive.file`. With it, the software can create files in your Google Drive and can see and change only the files it created. It cannot see any other file in your Drive.

## What the software stores in your Google Drive

The robot copies its study files into a "Talk with Reachy" folder in the Google Drive of the account that signed in on the robot:

- conversation transcripts with timestamps;
- audio clips of what people said to the robot;
- voice profiles that the robot uses to tell speakers apart;
- short notes the robot saved about individual speakers.

The same files are also kept on the robot. The robot keeps its Google sign-in in a file that only the robot's user account can read.

## What the developer receives

The developer does not run a server that receives Google user data. Files go directly from the robot to the signed-in Google Drive. Google user data is not sold, is not used for advertising, is not shared with third parties, and is not used to train AI models.

Talk with Reachy's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.

## Speech processing

To hold a conversation, the robot sends microphone audio to a speech service that Pollen Robotics hosts on Hugging Face. This is separate from the Google account and does not involve Google user data.

## Removing access and data

You can remove the software's access at any time at [myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions). Files the software created stay in your Drive until you delete them.

Participation in the study, and how study data is handled, is described in the study's consent materials.
